workingTitle: Two flashes eight years apart reveal a faraway companion
publicationStatus: Unreviewed arXiv preprint submitted to ApJL
coreFacts: OGLE-2016-BLG-0523 shows two short-lived microlensing bumps separated by 8.36 years.
The favored interpretation is a binary lens acting on one source star.
The two Einstein timescales are 8.343 plus or minus 0.076 days and 3.231 plus or minus 0.047 days.
The inferred binary mass ratio is about 0.15.
Bayesian analysis favors a low-mass M-dwarf primary with a low-mass brown-dwarf or super-Jupiter companion.
The inferred projected separation is about 450 astronomical units.
caveats: The paper is an unreviewed preprint.
The companion properties and projected separation are inferred through lens modeling and Bayesian analysis, not directly imaged.
Alternative scenarios were tested and disfavored, but microlensing degeneracies remain an important limitation.
